The bug is in SIP_RE: I wrote `"(" + UC + r"(?:%..."` — UC is a single char class without `+`, so the user part requires at least one literal char followed by escape groups... Actually UC alone matches exactly ONE char, then `(?:%HH UC)*` requires an escape before each subsequent char. So "inbox" fails.

Fix: user part = `UC+(?:%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}UC*)*` — hmm, need care: the general form is a sequence of (single allowed char | %HH). That's `(?:UC|%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2})+`. But then I must validate that the escapes decode to allowed chars. In norm_uri/decode_user I do that, but SIP_RE must enforce it too. Let me use the same trick as before with an explicit alternation of hex pairs that map to allowed chars. That's what USER_RE tried to do.

Simpler approach for the oracle: define ESC = a character class of valid two-hex-digit sequences? The set of allowed decoded chars is: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, `-`, `_`, `.`, `!`, `~`, `*`, `'`, `(`, `)`, `+`. Their hex codes: 41-5A, 61-7A, 30-39, 2D, 5F, 2E, 21, 7E, 2A, 27, 28, 29, 2B.

A regex alternation for the escape: `%(?:4[1-9A-F]|5[0-9A]|5[F]|6[1-9A-F]|7[A]|3[0-9]|2[D]|2[E]|2[1]|7[E]|2[A]|2[7]|2[8]|2[9]|2[B])`... messy. Let me instead build the escape alternation programmatically: list all hex pairs whose chr() is in the allowed set:

```python
ALLOWED = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-_.!~*'()+"
ESCS = "|".join("%{:02X}".format(ord(c)) + "|%{:02x}".format(ord(c)) for c in ALLOWED)
```
That's 63*2 = 126 alternatives — fine (a bit slow to compile, but ok). Better: build a regex for the escape using a character-class-free approach: `%[{hexchars}]{2}` then validate in code. Since the oracle's `norm_uri` can do the validation: match `USER_PART = (?:[allowed]|%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2})+` then in norm_uri check that every escape decodes into the allowed set. Let me restructure:

```python
USER_RE = re.compile(r"(?:[A-Za-z0-9\-_.!~*'()+]|%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2})+$")
SIP_RE = re.compile(r"sip:((?:[UC]|%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2})+)@(host)$", re.I)
```
and in norm_uri: after matching, verify each `%HH` decodes to an allowed char:
```python
for m in re.finditer(r"%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}", u):
    if chr(int(...)) not in ALLOWED: return None
```
Good. Let me rewrite the oracle's URI section cleanly.
